task_message:
Case L12: segment the lipomatous soft-tissue tumor on this T1-weighted MRI.

Volume: 281x281x249 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Case L12 is complete. Summary of what was done:

- **Finding the lesion:** Scanning axial/coronal/sagittal sheets revealed a large, lobulated fat-signal (T1-hyperintense) mass in the thigh, extending from near the hip/greater trochanter region down through the mid-thigh — a lipomatous soft-tissue tumor.
- **Initial mask:** Seeded with positive point prompts on the mass (axial 156, then axial 113 to capture the lateral component), producing a 3D segmentation of the fatty lesion.
- **Correction:** Morphological opening removed thin leaks along intermuscular fat planes near the femur and cleaned spurious components (112 → 2 components, tiny satellite only).
- **Checking:** Reviewed the mask in all three planes plus zoomed crops; used intensity-based candidates, all of which corresponded to the surrounding subcutaneous fat rim and were rejected.
- **Final review:** The five-slice-per-plane review showed the mask covering the lobulated mass with no tumor tissue in the past-the-end panels.
- **Saved:** Final mask, 673 mL, confidence medium — the main uncertainty is how far the tapering proximal pole extends toward the hip.
